summary: NZGDA annual survey observations span 2015-2025. Source units alternate between full-time employees, workers and FTEs, while respondents change. Later editions mention overseas staff. Keep snapshots and visa composition separate; no national index.

search_log.query: Statistics NZ ANZSIC game development workforce national employment
search_log.outcome: Stats NZ employment-indicator methodology inspected: broad industry categories, no separately identified game-development count. Ministry for Culture evidence brief also states codes historically could not directly measure games jobs and cites NZGDA. MBIE rebate review download did not return PDF; rebate cohort is not whole population.
Annual original NZGDA releases recovered; 2016 original release hosted by IGEA.

search_log.query: New Zealand game developers survey employees visas contractors
search_log.outcome: English local sources checked; current-versus-former visa status, overseas offices and contradictory 2024 count retained.

series.label: Survey full-time employees / roles
series.industry_scope: Games and interactive studios; later surveys explicitly include VR/AR, education technology and serious games. Contract development and studio services included; hardware, retail, venues and indirect employment not the intended scope.
series.occupation_scope: All roles in covered businesses, including creative, technical and business functions.
series.geography_note: New Zealand studios, all ownerships; 2017/18 explicitly workers in NZ studios. Later respondents include remote teams in NZ and overseas. 2024 reports 31 FTE Australia and 85 other overseas, without proving if included in headline. No subtraction made.
series.worker_status: Source wording shown per observation. Contractors, founders, agency staff, apprentices and interns not separately defined.
series.method: Annual voluntary association studio survey; sample sizes and source wording vary. No documented national gross-up or full-time-equivalence conversion across all years.
series.comparison_note: Fiscal years ending 31 March; reference-date exceptions in country notes. Variable samples and source units; no line trend or index. Overseas-office inclusion unresolved in later summaries.

limitations: Respondent pool varies from 27 studios in 2015 to 100 in 2024; 2025 response count not stated in release.
2019 workers are not automatically treated as 2019 FTEs.
Visa composition has changing definitions and rounded percentages; 2024 contains a 97/98 internal conflict.
Foreign ownership of studios is distinct from foreign citizenship and work abroad.
2015-2025 source-native observations are present; no claim of constant population or scope.
review_checks: Source metadata publication dates extracted separately from FY periods.
No annual headcount-to-FTE conversion or overseas subtraction.
